---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Do this before the first session"
---

Setup problems take a long time to fix during class, so please get ready **before** the first session.

## 1. Install R and an editor

-   **R** (version 4.1 or newer): <https://cran.r-project.org/>
-   **An editor**: [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/). Either works.

## 2. Install the R packages

Copy this into the R console and press Enter. It takes a few minutes.

```{r}
install.packages(c(
  # APIs
  "httr", "httr2", "jsonlite", "nhanesA", "tidycensus",
  # Web scraping
  "rvest", "xml2", "polite", "robotstxt",
  # Data cleaning and tables
  "tidyverse", "janitor", "flextable", "scales"
))
```

## 3. Get a Census API key (for Lesson 1)

The Census API needs a free key. It arrives by email within a few minutes.

1.  Request a key: <https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html>
2.  Open your `.Renviron` file:

    ```{r}
    file.edit("~/.Renviron")
    ```

3.  Add this line (with your key), save the file, and **restart R**:

    ``` text
    CENSUS_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY_HERE
    ```

::: callout-warning
## Keep your key private

Never paste API keys into your scripts, and never commit them to GitHub. Keeping them in `.Renviron` keeps them out of your code.
:::

## 4. Download the course folder

[⬇ Course folder (ZIP)](https://github.com/CWML/beyond-downloading/archive/refs/heads/main.zip){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}

Unzip it somewhere you can find it (not your Downloads folder). The demo files are:

-   `APIs/API_demonstration.qmd` (Lesson 1)
-   `web_scraping/web_scraping_demonstration.qmd` (Lesson 2)
-   `web_scraping/scraping_using_playwright.py` (Lesson 2, optional Python example)

## 5. (Optional) Python for dynamic scraping

The CDC FluView example in Lesson 2 uses Python and [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/). You only need this if you want to run that example yourself.

``` bash
pip install playwright pandas jupyter
playwright install chromium
```

::: callout-note
The Playwright script is written to run in a **Jupyter notebook** (it uses `await` at the top level). Paste it into a notebook cell rather than running `python scraping_using_playwright.py`.
:::

## 6. Test your setup

Run this in R. Each line should print the result in its comment.

```{r}
library(rvest)
read_html("https://example.com") |> html_element("h1") |> html_text2()
# [1] "Example Domain"

library(httr2)
request("https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/version") |> req_perform() |> resp_status()
# [1] 200

Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY") != ""
# [1] TRUE
```

If you see an error, email [maximilian.wegener@yale.edu](mailto:maximilian.wegener@yale.edu) before the first session.
